claims.sourceText: aaro.mil UAP Records page, accessed 12 August 2026
claims.text: AARO's UAP Records page directs the public to the National Archives UAP collection and hosts the DHS Kona Blue release and ORNL materials analyses.

b.label: AARO information papers (satellite flaring, forced perspective, 2025 UAP workshop, NPS CTX issue)

edges.label: Explanatory output on flaring, parallax, workshops and the NPS CTX issue
edges.note: AARO publishes analytic methodology continuously while withholding Volume II and its video holdings.

edges.label: AARO contracted ORNL in 2022 to test the magnesium alloy specimen
edges.note: AARO's own words: 'In 2022, The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) contracted with Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) to conduct materials testing on a magnesium (Mg) alloy specimen.'

edges.label: Council announced 17 June 2026, between Releases 03 and 04
edges.note: The council was announced as formed at the request of the White House and in coordination with AARO, ODNI, the FBI and other agencies, reporting to a higher-level UAP Governance Board.

a.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

edges.label: AARO points the public to NARA and asserts it is transferring records
edges.note: AARO's UAP Records page links first to the National Archives collection, and the Department states AARO has made progress transferring records in accordance with federal law.

b.label: AARO / ORNL Synopsis: Analysis of a Metallic Specimen

edges.label: Produced 'ORNL Synopsis: Analysis of a Metallic Specimen', April 2024
edges.note: Released publicly July 2024; concluded the material is a terrestrial magnesium alloy, while stating that neither AARO nor ORNL could verify the specimen's historical origin.

edges.label: AARO's founding director left government for the laboratory that analysed AARO's specimen
edges.note: Kirkpatrick departed AARO on 1 December 2023 and became Chief Technology Officer for Defense and Intelligence Programs at ORNL, a UT-Battelle laboratory that had supported AARO during his tenure.
